answer: Shared Attention Ledger. Each identity must periodically answer a randomly addressed query drawn from a live pulse of verified human work, and its answer is checked against a rolling knoll of consensus responses. An identity that misses or fails enough checks loses its routing priority at the next summit of the ledger's ranking. The scarce resource is sustained verified human attention over time, so an attacker running many sockpuppets must recruit and coordinate real workers for every identity, paying ongoing labor and coordination costs rather than a one-time fee.
